title: Swampland conjectures and the boundary of consistent quantum gravity
bottleneck: The swampland program conjectures that most low-energy effective field theories, including ones that look perfectly healthy, cannot be completed into a consistent quantum gravity theory, but the conjectures themselves remain unproven. There is no rigorous criterion separating the landscape of allowed theories from the swampland of forbidden ones.
why_it_blocks: Without a sharp boundary, model builders cannot know whether a proposed dark energy model, inflationary scenario, or particle extension is even compatible with quantum gravity, so entire research programs may rest on impossible foundations.
current_state: Conjectures such as the weak gravity conjecture and the de Sitter conjecture have survived many string-theory tests and rule out some simple models, but counterexamples and loopholes keep the program controversial and non-rigorous.
